segments.vo: Paying a token for a property? Ask for the encumbrance certificate first.
It's a record of registered transactions on that property, like sales or mortgages, for the period you ask for.
It can show you if the property is already mortgaged, or has been sold before.
Check that the owner's name and the property details match your agreement.
If something doesn't match, or the record has gaps, stop and ask why.
Then show it to your advocate before any money moves.
This is general guidance. Your advocate will tell you what applies to your property.
Save this before you pay a token.
